module_mood_contract: Day 1 vindication with a pulse: the craft you already respect, now steered by what you bring, set and ask; the unease is not voiced on Day 1 (Day 2 opens on it).

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: abstract claim told before the experience. L3 slide 'Same question, two answers' opens with a live contrast demo (ceiling/priming shown, vocabulary bring/set/ask taught mid-module at L5); sits after the box lecture and before the write-the-bet exercise (our-product-our-system.md L48-L52). Closest to violating: L5 names three moves before the student has used them, but each is operational vocabulary the next exercise uses, not a pattern-recognition closer.

Harm: lecturing steals the closer's felt evidence. Day 1 is vindication, not a contrast-mood module; the 10-minute lecture arms (L3 guess-and-reveal, L5 three moves, L7 plan-first) and names no practitioner or framework. Closest: L5 triad 'bring, set, ask' is a lens, one operational primitive per leg, no tradeoff reasoning.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -nE 'M[0-9]+|Module [0-9]' on expanded body above the maintainer fence -> 0 hits (planted 'M3 reads this' returns a hit).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L1: '# The agent knows only what you tell it' - truth clause: unsupported universal 'only'. The lecture itself shows the counter-example: slide 1 (via L3) has Claude answering Rome and Saimaa untold. Harm: a crisp false header is easier to believe and a cold-scanned handbook has no trainer voice to qualify it; harm present. Slide headers (L3, L5, L7, L9) pass squint and truth: each names a claim or named thing the body supports. Overlaps the writing judge's check_writing §21 row; one edit fixes both.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Qualify 'only' to what the body licenses: what you tell it shapes every answer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/apt101-only-what-you-tell-it.md -> 'oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A prompt inside a lecture is a trainer show-and-tell, never a room follow-along.
A new training's lectures start from the slide corpus, not from fresh prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L3-L9 are four include lines to curriculum/slides/*.md, no fork. Slide 1 is a generic borrow (reuse-map apt101-slide-reuse-map.md D1 row 'B'); slides 2-4 are APT101 rewrites (apt101-slide-reuse-map-v2.md L18, L20, L87: press-release and interview examples, no test/type-check). Closest: slide 1 is borrowed whole, but its Italy/Finland register is audience-neutral and not repeated in apt101-work-backwards (grep: only this lecture includes it).

Leaves the student: in control, her product knowledge is the lever (slide 2 'Each one needs someone who knows the product'; slide 4 'You hold what it hasn't got'); sets up write-the-bet. Day 1 contract (our-product-our-system.md L105): vindication, unease not voiced. Trace phases 8/8/8/8, close 8. Closest to low: slide 3 (L7) is the most operational beat, still a teaching beat at 8.

Closest: slide 4 'a feature you dropped last year, a quote nobody said' names an error the agent makes, framed as the agent's fill and 'the gap is worth a look', never as the team's mistake; 'your team never wrote that one down' is a prompt to write it, not a blame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Headers name disciplines (steer, plan first, you are the check). Failure mode appears only in slide 4 body as the negative case the discipline addresses; no failure-word titles.

Facets: front-run - slide 4 names 'a quote nobody said' as one of three invented fills; Day 2 owns the invented-quote stance and exercise (a-customer-need-nobody-said, apt101-catch-it-making-things-up), but Day 1 plants it as an example under 'you are the check' without the 'most dangerous' stance or the fits-the-favourite-hypothesis amplify mechanism (three-ways-to-steer maintainer: not stated on Day 1). Slide 2 'a second agent with a different brief' plants the Day 2/3 judge, does not teach building one. Arc: squint order L25-L29 matches the file order exactly; follows work-backwards, hands to write-the-bet. Mood not resolved early: no verification step resolves Day 2 unease. Big Idea: Day 1 'you were right all along' honoured (control through what you bring, set, ask).
